issuer: Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District
text: HEALTH ADVISORY: Waterborne Disease Cluster — Districts 3 and 4. The Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District is investigating an elevated number of cases of acute gastrointestinal illness, including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps, among residents of Water Districts 3 and 4. As of today, Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center have treated more than 600 patients with these symptoms since September 29, the majority of whom reside in Districts 3 and 4. Laboratory tests have confirmed the presence of Cryptosporidium and Giardia — waterborne parasites — in multiple patient samples. These findings are consistent with consumption of untreated water. All residents in Districts 3 and 4 must continue to boil all water used for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, and making ice until further notice. Boil water vigorously for two minutes before use. If you are experiencing severe dehydration, bloody diarrhea, or are immunocompromised, seek emergency medical care immediately. Additional information will be provided as the investigation continues. For questions, call the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District line: 361-826-7200.

text: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has confirmed that it is investigating anomalous access to internal network systems that may have occurred during the Hurricane Rafael response period. CBPWA's Security Operations Center identified unusual access patterns in network logs and has opened a formal security review in coordination with Vantage Security Systems, our SIEM and security technology partner. At this time there is no indication that customer data has been affected. CBPWA is working closely with relevant federal and state agencies. Additional information will be provided as the investigation progresses. CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna is leading the investigation.

CLEANUP MILESTONE — October 4, 2027: Unified Command announces that the main oil slick from the September 14 Inner Harbor discharge is contained. Primary skimming operations have concluded with recovery of approximately 142,000 gallons of oil-water mixture. TCEQ monitoring readings in Corpus Christi Bay have declined to an average of 0.40 milligrams per liter, down from a peak of 3.4 mg/L recorded on September 17. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant raw water intake has returned to below the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold and is operating normally. Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue reports 340 oiled birds documented through today; 198 birds have been successfully rehabilitated and released. Shoreline cleanup operations in Nueces Bay are ongoing, with hand crews working approximately 6.4 kilometers of affected shoreline. The response is moving from emergency containment to shoreline cleanup. Fishing and shellfish harvesting closures in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays remain in effect pending state testing. Joint Information Center: (361) 555-0147.

text: The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency are investigating unauthorized access to control systems at a Corpus Christi utility. Texas Cyber Command has been activated to assist. The Governor has directed all critical infrastructure operators in the state to review remote-access security procedures and report any anomalies to CISA. This investigation is active and ongoing; no further operational details will be released at this time.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation today announced a joint investigation into anomalous activity affecting industrial control systems at a coastal electric utility in Texas during the Hurricane Rafael response period. The activity was identified during routine review of utility incident reports submitted under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act. CISA and FBI are working with the affected utility and state partners to assess the scope, origin, and impact of the activity. No attribution has been made at this time. Utilities in the Gulf Coast region are encouraged to review and implement CISA's operational technology security guidelines and report anomalous ICS activity through the CISA 24/7 operations center. This investigation is ongoing and additional information will be provided as appropriate.

TDEM interim after-action snapshot on public communications during Hurricane Rafael: 'Communication timelines in Spanish showed variation from English baseline. Recommend review of NCLAS contract performance.'

The Texas Division of Emergency Management today released a first after-action snapshot on public communications during Hurricane Rafael. It notes 'observed delays in Spanish-language alert distribution' but gives no figures and makes no recommendations. Separately, a local chapter of the League of United Latin American Citizens filed a complaint with the state citing its limited-English-proficiency plan and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. KNCB Coastal Bend Radio read the complaint on the air.

issuer: FEMA Joint Field Office Corpus Christi / Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
text: JOINT STATEMENT — October 5, 2027: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Joint Field Office and the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority are issuing this statement regarding the extended power outages affecting Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael. While the initial power outages were caused by wind and storm surge damage to the CBPWA transmission and distribution network, investigators from the federal government and CBPWA have determined that the duration of outages in certain districts was extended by deliberate interference with utility control systems beyond what storm damage alone would have caused. This determination was made following a technical review of utility operational data by federal investigators. The investigation is ongoing. CBPWA has implemented enhanced security measures for its control systems and is working with federal partners to prevent future incidents. No decision has been made on whether residents who experienced prolonged outages will be eligible for additional disaster assistance. Power has been restored to most customers; restoration in parts of northwest and central Corpus Christi is continuing while relay inspection and repair are completed. CBPWA urges any customer with information relevant to this investigation to contact the FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency at (361) 555-0100.

text: Complaint TX-DEM-2027-LEP-0012 filed with the Texas Division of Emergency Management alleges violations of Texas LEP Plan Section 4.2 (simultaneous multi-language release for life-safety alerts) and Title VI, 42 U.S.C. 2000d, in the release of emergency alerts during Hurricane Rafael.

issuer: Texas Department of State Health Services
text: The Texas Department of State Health Services has completed a preliminary investigation into the waterborne disease outbreak affecting Corpus Christi Water Districts 3 and 4. DSHS has confirmed that Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia are the causative agents of the outbreak. Both pathogens are transmitted exclusively through contaminated water. The investigation determined that exposure occurred during the period of low water pressure in Districts 3 and 4 following Hurricane Rafael, consistent with the Boil Water Notice issued by the City of Corpus Christi on September 26, 2027. DSHS is coordinating with the City of Corpus Christi, Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority, and the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District on the ongoing public health response. The Boil Water Notice for Districts 3 and 4 remains in effect. Residents should continue to boil all water before consumption. DSHS advises all immunocompromised individuals, infants, and elderly residents in the affected area to contact their healthcare provider if they have experienced any gastrointestinal symptoms.

CISA has issued Emergency Directive 27-02 directing all federal agencies operating industrial control systems to audit remote-access credentials and configuration change logs within 72 hours. The directive follows a confirmed ICS incident at a Texas utility in which a threat actor gained access via compromised remote-access credentials and made unauthorized changes to operational technology systems. Owners and operators of critical infrastructure are strongly encouraged to review CISA Advisory AA27-266A for indicators and mitigations.

text: Governor has amended the existing Hurricane Rafael disaster declaration to include a cyber emergency component covering Corpus Christi utility infrastructure. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has deployed a cybersecurity rapid response team to assist local and state authorities. The affected utility has isolated its control systems as a precautionary measure; field crews are managing operations manually. The Governor's office emphasized that the water supply remains safe for boiled use and that electric restoration continues.

The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today reported that Hurricane Rafael emergency call volume has returned to near-normal levels, with 380 calls received yesterday — approaching the pre-storm daily baseline of 310 calls. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss said the center is beginning a transition back to normal staffing over the next two weeks. 'Our dispatchers have shown extraordinary dedication over the past four weeks. The scale and duration of this response was unprecedented for our center, and I am incredibly proud of every person who answered calls, coordinated rescues, and kept working through the most demanding conditions I have seen in my career.' Director Escamilla-Voss noted that CBECC handled more than 44,200 calls in the four weeks after landfall, about five times the normal volume. The center is retaining all call records and audio as part of its standard after-action review process. Mutual aid units from San Patricio and Bee County will begin scaling back their support beginning October 14.

Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has taken precautionary steps to isolate portions of its operational technology network following the identification of unauthorized access to network systems. These measures are being taken as part of an ongoing security investigation. The isolation is expected to cause no disruption to power or water service for CBPWA customers. CBPWA is cooperating with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and other relevant authorities. CBPWA emphasizes that the investigation is ongoing and no conclusions should be drawn about the nature or origin of the access at this time.

TDI ACTIVATES CLAIMS FRAUD TASK FORCE — October 14, 2027: Texas Department of Insurance Commissioner announces the activation of a Disaster Claims Fraud Task Force for Nueces County following Hurricane Rafael. The task force, operating in coordination with the FBI and Texas DPS, will focus on detecting and preventing fraudulent insurance claims arising from the storm. TDI has identified patterns of concern including clusters of large commercial property claims with similar damage narratives, inflated pre-storm appraisals, and claims for total losses on properties that sustained only partial damage. TDI emphasizes that filing a fraudulent insurance claim is a third-degree felony in Texas, punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and fines up to $10,000. Insurers are reminded of their obligation to refer suspected fraud to TDI's Fraud Unit. TDI is working with the Insurance Council of Texas to establish a Nueces County claims database to identify duplicate and suspicious claims across carriers. Legitimate policyholders are encouraged to cooperate with claim investigations and to report any third party who pressured them into filing inflated claims.

issuer: Texas Department of Insurance / Insurance Council of Texas
text: DISASTER CLAIMS SURGE UPDATE — October 14, 2027: The Texas Department of Insurance and the Insurance Council of Texas report that Hurricane Rafael has generated approximately 187,000 property insurance claims across Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties as of October 14, representing an estimated $2.1 billion in insured losses. This ranks as the second-largest coastal insured loss event in Texas since Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Claims volume in the Corpus Christi metropolitan area exceeds industry catastrophe response models by approximately 23 percent. TDI has activated its Disaster Response Team and deployed 12 field claim examiners. The department notes an elevated pattern of large commercial property claims in Districts 3-5 that is under review. Adjusters are reporting difficulty verifying pre-storm property values in certain commercial portfolios. Homeowners and commercial property owners are reminded that Texas law requires insurers to acknowledge claims within 15 days and pay or deny within 15 business days of receiving all claim documentation. Residents experiencing claim delays should contact TDI at (800) 252-3439. TDI is tracking contractor fraud complaints and coordinating with the Texas DPS.

The Port of Corpus Christi Authority announced today that the Corpus Christi Ship Channel has partly reopened to commercial traffic, 30 days after Hurricane Rafael closed it. The Coast Guard cleared the outer and bay reaches of the channel after surveys of channel depth and aids to navigation. The inner channel remains restricted while vessels and berths affected by the Inner Harbor oil spill are decontaminated; no date has been set for lifting that restriction. Ships waiting at the offshore anchorage will be brought in by priority, and the backlog will delay some cargo, including relief shipments. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves said: 'We are grateful for the patience of our customers and maritime partners. The port team, together with the Coast Guard, NOAA and our contractor crews, worked extraordinary hours to restore safe navigation after one of the most demanding storm responses in our history.' Six port security cameras along the Inner Harbor remain offline pending replacement parts. The Coast Guard investigation into the tanker oil release remains open.

issuer: Port of Corpus Christi Authority / CBPWA joint statement
text: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority today announced a joint counter-unmanned aircraft initiative for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor, following a recommendation in the FAA-CBP joint report on pre-storm unauthorized drone activity. The initiative will deploy an RF-sensing detection and direction-finding network at multiple sites across the port and utility infrastructure corridor, operated in coordination with the FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations. Sentinel Airspace Inc. has been selected as the technology provider following a competitive evaluation. The network is expected to be operational within 90 days. Port Director Marcus Obianwu-Kelley and CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna jointly signed the agreement.

The Texas Division of Emergency Management, working with federal partners, has identified and referred to law enforcement a network of social media accounts that disseminated false public safety information during Hurricane Rafael. The accounts distributed incorrect evacuation shelter locations, false road closure information, and misleading content about utility restoration and federal investigations. TDEM's social media monitoring tool, Coastal Alert, detected anomalous posting behavior consistent with coordinated inauthentic behavior. TDEM has referred account information to the FBI and has coordinated with social media platforms on account review. Members of the public who encountered false shelter or evacuation information during the Rafael response are asked to report it to TDEM's public information line at 512-424-2208. TDEM reminds the public to verify emergency information through official sources: NuecesCountyOEM.org, 2-1-1 Texas, and local broadcast stations designated in the Corpus Christi Emergency Alert System.

text: Two major social media platforms announced Friday the removal of 847 accounts engaged in coordinated inauthentic behavior related to Hurricane Rafael public safety communications. The companies said the accounts had spread false evacuation shelter locations, fabricated road closure reports, and promoted misleading claims about the cause of extended power outages in Corpus Christi. The platforms said the accounts showed 'clear indicators of artificial coordination' including synchronized posting times, shared infrastructure, and near-identical content across different handles. The joint announcement followed referrals from the Texas Division of Emergency Management and the FBI's Cyber Division. Neither platform attributed the network to a specific actor or government. Texas Attorney General spokesperson Brandon Lacey-Rhinehart said the state was 'continuing to investigate the origin and intent of this coordinated effort to undermine public safety during a natural disaster.' The discovery of the false shelter posts is of particular concern: Nueces County OEM confirmed that at least 23 residents called the county 211 line on the day before landfall asking about Zavala Elementary as a shelter location, based on social media posts that have since been removed.

issuer: Texas Office of the Attorney General
text: The Office of the Texas Attorney General today issued a consumer advisory warning Texans about misinformation campaigns targeting emergency communications during natural disasters. During Hurricane Rafael, coordinated social media accounts posted false information including incorrect evacuation shelter addresses, fabricated road closure reports, and misleading claims about the causes of utility outages in the Corpus Christi area. The OAG advises Texans to: verify emergency information only through official government websites and designated emergency broadcast stations; report suspected misinformation to local emergency management or through the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3.gov); and be cautious of social media accounts with limited post history that suddenly begin posting high volumes of local emergency content. The OAG is cooperating with the FBI's ongoing investigation into the organized distribution of false public safety information during the Rafael response period.

Sabal Energy Wire has obtained documents confirming that the prolonged power outages affecting portions of Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael were partly attributable to unauthorized modifications to protective relay settings at two CBPWA substations. The modifications, discovered during a security investigation that began October 2nd, caused affected relay groups to tolerate fault currents above their designed trip thresholds, extending grid restoration timelines by an estimated 11 to 18 days. CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna declined to comment on specific findings, citing an ongoing investigation. CISA confirmed that ICS-CERT advisory ICS-2027-CC-00441 covers incidents of this type.

The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today formally closed its Hurricane Rafael surge response posture and returned to standard staffing levels. Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss announced that CBECC has established a partnership with Nueces County Information Technology to preserve the call record archive from landfall through October 29 for training and after-action analysis purposes. The archive covers more than 56,000 calls in English and Spanish and represents the most complete 911 call record ever retained for a Gulf Coast storm response. Director Escamilla-Voss also announced a new 911 abuse reporting tip line, 1-800-NUECES-9, for residents to report suspected false emergency reports. 'During any major emergency, bad actors sometimes attempt to abuse the emergency communications system to divert rescuers,' said Escamilla-Voss. 'We take this seriously, and we ask the public to help us protect the integrity of 911 by reporting suspected abuse.' The NuecesInfoLine, opened during the boil-water notices, will close on Friday, November 5. CBECC thanks the residents of Districts 3 and 4 for their patience during the extended water notices.

FEMA Region 6 announced today the completion of the Hurricane Rafael Aerial Assessment Program, the most comprehensive post-storm aerial survey conducted in the Texas Gulf Coast region. From a pre-storm baseline on September 12 through October 29, federal, state, and contracted aerial assets generated more than 6.2 million georeferenced image tiles covering 183 square kilometers of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area. The imagery archive spans all phases of the disaster cycle from pre-storm baseline through active recovery. Beginning today, downsampled imagery from Phase 1 and Phase 2 surveys is publicly available through the FEMA OpenData portal for use by academic researchers, local governments, and community organizations engaged in recovery planning. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park stated: 'This imagery archive is a resource that will support not just today's recovery, but future preparedness for the entire Texas Gulf Coast. We are grateful to NOAA, the Texas Army National Guard, and our contracted partners for executing this mission under difficult post-storm conditions.' Requests for access to full-resolution imagery should be directed to FEMA Region 6 Geospatial Programs at the contact listed below.

KNCB Coastal Bend Radio news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega testified before the Nueces County Commissioners Court today regarding gaps in bilingual emergency communications during Hurricane Rafael. Fuentes-Vega presented broadcast logs documenting delays between English and Spanish public alerts across four alert categories during the Rafael response: mandatory evacuation orders (2 hours 47 minutes), shelter-in-place guidance (7 hours 52 minutes), boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (12 hours 33 minutes), and power restoration status announcements (average 9 hours 11 minutes). The average delay across all categories was 8 hours 6 minutes. Commissioners voted 4–1 to direct the county's Office of Emergency Management to issue a new Request for Proposals for language access services requiring simultaneous multi-language alert release within 30 minutes for all life-safety notifications.
